item.title: The economic outlook and some thoughts on labor market dynamism

rating.summary: Governor Waller outlines a clearly hawkish policy stance, noting that while the labor market is stable and near maximum employment, inflation remains well above the 2 percent target with broad-based price pressures. He signals support for a 25 basis point rate hike at the December FOMC meeting as a baseline, with an open door to 50 basis points if incoming CPI data disappoint. He also discusses structural concerns about declining labor market dynamism and its longer-run implications for productivity and inflation.
rating.stance_rationale: Waller explicitly states further tightening is needed 'sooner rather than later,' pre-commits to a December hike, and raises the possibility of a 50 bps move if inflation data are worse than expected, reflecting a strongly hawkish posture with upside risk to the rate path.
key_quotes: I believe further tightening of monetary policy will be needed, sooner rather than later, to return inflation to a path that will reach 2 percent in the medium term.

If the October CPI inflation data out later today are similar to the past two monthly readings—with core CPI inflation around 0.3 percent or even higher—then a stronger policy move may be needed. In that case, I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting.
